title: Envelope
description: Every frame is one JSON object with this envelope. Receivers ignore unknown fields.

id.description: Message id: c_ + ULID from the console, n_ + ULID from the daemon.

seq.description: Only on reliable messages: monotonically increasing per sender within one node.

Ack.title: Ack
Ack.description: Cumulative ACK: every reliable message with seq <= N has been durably processed. Sent at least every 200 ms or every 50 messages.

ApprovalAck.title: ApprovalAck
ApprovalAck.description: The daemon applied approval.resolve (stale = the pending request no longer existed).

ApprovalCancel.title: ApprovalCancel
ApprovalCancel.description: A pending approval went away; the console marks the card cancelled.

ApprovalRequest.title: ApprovalRequest
ApprovalRequest.description: canUseTool / Codex requestApproval needs a decision.

suggestions.description: SDK PermissionUpdate[], stored verbatim and returned on allow_always.

message.description: Shown to the model on deny.

OpenGen.title: OpenGen
OpenGen.description: How many times the session has been opened; +1 on every resume.

ImageRef.title: ImageRef
ImageRef.description: An image the user attached to a message (at_attachments). The daemon downloads it with GET <console>/nodes/attachments/<id> and its node token, then hands it to the runtime: Claude gets an image content block (a document block for a PDF), Codex a localImage input item (a PDF is saved and its path named in the text).

CallId.title: CallId
CallId.description: Platform tool call id: tc_ + ULID, generated by the daemon.

UploadId.title: UploadId
UploadId.description: File upload id (up_ + ULID), generated by the daemon.

DownloadId.title: DownloadId
DownloadId.description: File download id (dn_ + id), generated by the console for read_deliverable and read_shared_file.

RelPath.title: RelPath
RelPath.description: Path relative to the daemon root; never absolute.

PermissionMode.title: PermissionMode
PermissionMode.description: Claude permission mode; always explicit. The console opens writing members in bypassPermissions (with allow_dangerously_skip_permissions) or default (ask roles), and the coordinator, lead and read-only roles in dontAsk. auto is kept for old consoles only.

ContextUsage.title: ContextUsage
ContextUsage.description: How much of the context window a session uses (shared-members.md §5.3).

used_tokens.description: Tokens in the context now (Claude: getContextUsage totalTokens; Codex: the last request's total tokens).

max_tokens.description: The window the runtime measures against (Claude: the autocompact window; Codex: the model's context window); 0 when unknown.

SshServer.title: SshServer
SshServer.description: A remote server a session may reach through the console's SSH gateway (remote-servers.md §7). name is the server's name in the owner's settings and the Host alias in the session's ssh_config.

CredRequest.title: CredRequest
CredRequest.description: Credential helper asks for a short-lived token. Unreliable, retried after 10 s with the same req_id; never logged.

force_refresh.description: Git rejected the token handed out last (credential erase): the console skips its token cache and mints a new one (at most once a minute per token scope).

CredResponse.title: CredResponse
CredResponse.description: Token for a cred.request, or a refusal. Unreliable; never logged.

ref_id.description: Envelope id of the offending message.

FileChunk.title: FileChunk
FileChunk.description: One piece of a file upload (publish_file, write_shared_file). Chunks are sent before the tool.call that references their upload_id; the console keeps them until that call assembles them.

index.description: 0-based position of this chunk in the upload (all files concatenated in tool.call upload.files order).

FileDownload.title: FileDownload
FileDownload.description: One piece of the files read_deliverable or read_shared_file sends to the employee's working directory. Chunks are sent before the tool.result that references their download_id (download or shared_download); the daemon keeps them for that call only, checks sizes and checksums, and writes the files under .agent-deliverables/ (read_deliverable) or .shared/ (read_shared_file).

index.description: 0-based position of this chunk in the download (all files concatenated in tool.result download.files order).

GitCleanup.title: GitCleanup
GitCleanup.description: Remove worktrees (keeping unpushed work when asked) and prune.

GitPrepare.title: GitPrepare
GitPrepare.description: Clone the shared repo and/or add the worktree (architecture.md 8.1). Idempotent. With sync, an existing worktree is brought up to date before a task starts (shared-members.md 4.2).

base.description: Branch to create from when branch does not exist yet.

sync.description: Bring an existing worktree up to date (daemon feature git.sync). member: fetch, then switch to the member branch if needed, fast-forward it to origin/<ref> when it has no commits outside it and the tree is clean, else merge origin/<ref> into it (abort on conflict). review: fetch and check out origin/<ref> detached (read-only review of another member's branch), or expect_sha when given. A worktree that does not exist yet is created first, then synced.

ref.description: Remote branch name without origin/: the thread branch (member) or the branch under review (review).

deadline.description: Skip the sync (action expired) when the job starts after this time: the console has already sent the task brief and the member may be working in the tree.

expect_sha.description: review (daemon feature git_review_sha): the commit under review. The daemon fetches again (a few times, before the deadline) until it has the commit, checks it out detached and verifies HEAD; when it cannot, the job fails with error_code sha_mismatch and head_sha set to the actual HEAD.

GitPurge.title: GitPurge
GitPurge.description: Delete a whole project directory, or one thread's directory (projects/<pid>/threads/<no>, thread deleted), once no session is active there.

GitPush.title: GitPush
GitPush.description: Push an employee branch of one repository with a one-job write token; refspec target must be refs/heads/thread/<thread_no>/<employee>.

force_with_lease.description: Expected remote sha; only for member branches after conflict repair.

unchanged_against.description: Branches (thread branch, base) whose commits are not the employee's work: when HEAD has no commit outside them the push is skipped and the result says unchanged.

created.description: git.prepare: the worktree/clone was created by this job.

unchanged.description: git.push: nothing to push (no commits outside unchanged_against); head_sha is the checkout's HEAD.

sync.description: git.prepare with sync: what the sync did.

action.description: reset: member branch fast-forwarded to origin/<ref>; merged: origin/<ref> merged into unmerged member commits; conflict: that merge conflicted and was aborted; dirty: uncommitted changes, nothing done; checkout: review checkout; current: already up to date; absent: origin/<ref> does not exist (yet); expired: started after the deadline, nothing done.

GitStatus.title: GitStatus
GitStatus.description: Report branch/ahead/behind/dirty state of a checkout.

Hello.title: Hello
Hello.description: First frame from the daemon after connecting.

protocols.description: Supported protocol versions, highest priority first.

epoch.description: Outbox epoch; changes only when the state directory is wiped.

last_seq.description: Highest seq sent in this epoch.

acked_cmd_seq.description: Highest console command seq executed and persisted.

features.description: Feature names, e.g. sessions, codex_app_server, git_worktree, git_sync, cred_helper, upgrade, file_download (read_deliverable file.download), shared_files (write_shared_file upload and read_shared_file shared_download into .shared/), context_usage (turn_ended carries context), session_compact (session.compact), usage (node.usage), ssh_gateway (session.open ssh_servers, ssh.cert_request, ssh.servers_update, /nodes/ssh).

ssh_client.description: OpenSSH client on the node (ssh -V), when found.

Log.title: Log
Log.description: Daemon log line, warn and above only; unreliable.

NodeConfig.title: NodeConfig
NodeConfig.description: Settings changed on the node page, pushed immediately.

NodeDrain.title: NodeDrain
NodeDrain.description: Stop accepting new sessions and park idle ones (maintenance).

NodeStats.title: NodeStats
NodeStats.description: Every 30 s, unreliable; drives the server-room rack lights.

NodeUpgrade.title: NodeUpgrade
NodeUpgrade.description: Upgrade the daemon. The download URL is fixed: <console>/node/dist/agent-teams-node-<version>.tgz; sha256 and the Ed25519 release signature are verified.

signature.description: Base64 Ed25519 signature of the tgz.

NodeUpgradeResult.title: NodeUpgradeResult
NodeUpgradeResult.description: Upgrade failure report (success shows up as a reconnect with the new version).

auth.description: How the runtime is logged in: subscription (Claude), chatgpt (Codex), api_key, or none.

status.description: ok: windows are valid; error: fetching failed (see error); unsupported: no quota for this login (API key, not logged in, too old CLI).

plan.description: Plan name when known (pro, max, plus, team, ...).

windows.description: At most 8 are kept by the console.

fetched_at.description: When the daemon fetched this data.

key.description: five_hour, weekly, weekly_opus, weekly_sonnet, weekly_model (per-model weekly window, see label) (Claude); primary, secondary (Codex).

label.description: Display name given by the provider, e.g. the model of a weekly_model window; the console keeps at most 40 characters.

used_percent.description: 0..100; the console clamps values out of range.

NodeUsage.title: NodeUsage
NodeUsage.description: Subscription quota of the node's runtimes (Claude Code, Codex), unreliable; sent after hello and then periodically. Never carries credentials. The console keeps only the latest report per node and drops unknown fields.

NodeUsageRefresh.title: NodeUsageRefresh
NodeUsageRefresh.description: Fetch the subscription quota now and answer with node.usage (unreliable). Sent only when hello.features contains usage.

forget.description: Also delete the local session record (SDK transcript is kept 7 days).

SessionCompact.title: SessionCompact
SessionCompact.description: Compact the session's context now (between tasks, shared-members.md §5.3). The daemon runs it when the session is between turns and answers session.compacted; the stored task anchor is cleared (the task it belonged to is over).

compact_id.description: Chosen by the console; session.compacted echoes it.

instructions.description: What the summary must keep (Claude: /compact <instructions>; Codex has no instructions and ignores it).

SessionCompacted.title: SessionCompacted
SessionCompacted.description: session.compact finished (ok=false: the runtime did not compact; error says why, e.g. busy: the session stayed in a turn or got a new message first, exited: the runtime ended during the compaction, restarted: the daemon restarted before it finished).

SessionDelivered.title: SessionDelivered
SessionDelivered.description: session.send was pushed into the session.

SessionEvent.title: SessionEvent
SessionEvent.description: Session activity event; which fields are present depends on kind (protocol.md 4.8).

tools.description: turn_started: tool list from this turn's init, re-checked by the console.

text.description: text: assistant text, truncated to 8 KB.

category.description: tool_started: edit | read | shell | web | platform | other.

summary.description: tool_started / tool_ended: secret-free summary (Bash command truncated to 200 chars).

model.description: turn_ended: the model that answered the turn (Claude: the model of the turn's last main-agent assistant message; Codex: the model the turn ran with).

usage.description: turn_ended: token usage as reported by the runtime.

context.description: turn_ended: context use after the turn (daemons with feature context_usage).

todos.description: todos: the employee's whole checklist after a TodoWrite (latest state).

plan.description: plan: the Markdown plan of an ExitPlanMode call, truncated to 32 KB.

queued_msg_ids.description: Messages still queued in the SDK, mapped back to msg_id.

thread_no.description: The thread the session works in; null for the coordinator and a project member outside any thread.

scope.description: Where the employee belongs: "project" for the coordinator and the project members shared by every thread (skills and plugins live in <project>/project/<name>), "thread" for a lead or a member created with a thread. Absent from older consoles: a null thread_no means project.

tools.description: SDK options.tools; [] means no built-in tools.

allow_dangerously_skip_permissions.description: Required for bypassPermissions and session.set_mode to bypassPermissions.

read_only.description: Lead and read_only roles: enables bash_policy and a sandbox without writable paths.

deny_non_platform_tools.description: Coordinator: PreToolUse hook rejects everything except mcp__platform__*.

BashPolicy.title: BashPolicy
BashPolicy.description: argv-parsed allow list for read-only sessions (not regex).

config.description: Extra thread/start config (e.g. sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots); mcp_servers.platform is filled in by the daemon.

images.description: Images to deliver with the text (at most 8).

anchor.description: The task anchor, as session.send anchor.

files.description: Text files of the skill; SKILL.md is required.

path.description: Relative path inside the skill directory.

version.description: Library version number (1, 2, …); the directory is <name>@<version>.

files.description: Every file of the package, .claude-plugin/plugin.json included.

skills.description: Qualified names (<plugin>:<skill or command>) to add to options.skills.

mcp_servers.description: The plugin's MCP servers by name; ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is replaced by the plugin directory.

path.description: Relative path inside the plugin directory; '.' and '..' segments are refused.

encoding.description: utf8 (default) or base64 for binary files.

SessionOpen.title: SessionOpen
SessionOpen.description: Open (or resume) a long-lived employee session on the node. ssh_servers: remote servers granted to the employee's role in this project (remote-servers.md §7), sent only when both sides have the ssh_gateway feature; omitted or empty means no SSH access.

prepare.description: Key of the git.prepare job that must have succeeded first.

prepare_jobs.description: Every git.prepare job (one per repository) that must have succeeded first; prepare is the first of them.

env.description: Extra non-secret environment; the daemon adds PATH/HOME/MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT/git credential variables itself.

context.description: Context management of the role (shared-members.md §5.1): the runtime compacts by itself at limit_tokens × in_task_pct / 100 (Codex: limit_tokens capped at window_tokens). Without limit_tokens the target is in_task_pct of window_tokens; without either, Codex keeps its own default and Claude applies in_task_pct to its effective window (window − 20K). Claude never compacts later than its effective window − 13K. focus is added to the instructions of such a compaction.

limit_tokens.description: The role's context limit in tokens.

window_tokens.description: The context window the runtime reported for this employee's last session (tokens), when known. Codex caps limit_tokens at it (a limit above the model's window would never trigger); without limit_tokens both runtimes take in_task_pct of it as the token target.

git_credentials.description: Install the credential helper and gh wrapper.

anchor.description: The anchor of the task the employee holds when the session (re)opens without a first_message anchor (a crash reopen, a reopen after a daemon restart): the new process starts with it, as if session.send had carried it.

skills.description: Skills of the employee's role. Claude: the daemon writes them as a local plugin outside the worktree and loads it (options.plugins + options.skills). Codex gets them in developer_instructions instead.

plugins.description: Plugins ticked on the employee's role, each at an exact version (architecture.md §6.5). The daemon writes each into a per-employee directory outside the worktree. Claude: loaded with options.plugins (skipMcpDiscovery), skills lists the plugin's skills and commands, and mcp_servers join options.mcpServers as plugin_<plugin>_<server>. Codex: only mcp_servers are used (the skill text is already in developer_instructions).

commands.description: Slash commands the session offers besides Claude Code's own (role skills, plugin skills and commands), from initializationResult().commands without the builtin ones. Absent for Codex.

resume_failed.description: resume could not find the transcript/thread; the console runs the hand-over flow.

SessionRelease.title: SessionRelease
SessionRelease.description: Tool check passed: the daemon may push first_message and queued messages for this open_gen.

SessionSend.title: SessionSend
SessionSend.description: Deliver a message to the employee.

images.description: Images to deliver with the text (at most 8).

anchor.description: The task anchor (task id, instruction, branch, hand-off notes, progress). The daemon keeps the latest one and re-injects it after the runtime compacts the session during a task; an empty string clears it.

SessionSetMode.title: SessionSetMode
SessionSetMode.description: Change permission mode and/or model of a session.

SessionWatch.title: SessionWatch
SessionWatch.description: Turn stream.delta on/off while someone watches live output.

SessionsReport.title: SessionsReport
SessionsReport.description: Sessions currently present on the node; the orchestrator reconciles against it.

SshCertRequest.title: SshCertRequest
SshCertRequest.description: The session's ssh-agent needs a certificate for its in-memory key (remote-servers.md §4.2–4.5). Unreliable, req_id; the console checks the session belongs to this node with this open_gen (§2.3) and answers ssh.cert_response. Never logged.

public_key.description: The session's ephemeral public key, one OpenSSH authorized_keys line (ssh-ed25519 AAAA…).

SshCertResponse.title: SshCertResponse
SshCertResponse.description: Answer to ssh.cert_request: a user certificate signed by the session CA, or a refusal. Unreliable; never logged. servers: the servers the session may use now (granted to its role); the daemon rewrites ssh_config with them and they are the certificate's principals.

certificate.description: OpenSSH certificate, one line (ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com AAAA…); principals are the server names in servers.

known_hosts.description: known_hosts lines for the gateway host key, written to the session's known_hosts.

error.description: e.g. session_not_found, stale_open_gen, no_servers, not_granted, bad_public_key, rate_limited (more than 20 certificates a minute for the session), unavailable.

SshServersUpdate.title: SshServersUpdate
SshServersUpdate.description: The servers a live session may use changed (a server added, removed or renamed in the project, a role grant changed). The daemon rewrites the session's ssh_config atomically and drops its current certificate (the next use asks for a new one). Also sent once per live session after a node reconnects. version grows per session; an older version than the last applied is ignored. An empty servers list: the session has no server any more (remove ssh_config).

StreamDelta.title: StreamDelta
StreamDelta.description: Unreliable token stream, only while session.watch is on; not stored.

chunks.description: Number of file.chunk frames (0 when every file is empty).

path.description: publish_file: path inside the published deliverable (index.html for a site's entry, or the file name). write_shared_file: exactly one file, and path is the target shared-files path (args.path, or the default the daemon derived from args.file).

ToolCall.title: ToolCall
ToolCall.description: An employee called a platform tool.

tool.description: Platform tool name without the mcp__platform__ prefix.

args.description: Tool input; validated by the console against /protocol/schemas/tools/<tool>.json.

tool_use_id.description: Claude tool_use_id or Codex item id, for diagnostics only.

upload.description: Files the daemon read for publish_file or write_shared_file; their bytes arrived before as file.chunk frames.

ToolCancel.title: ToolCancel
ToolCancel.description: A blocking tool call was abandoned (interrupt, close or process restart).

chunks.description: Number of file.download frames (0 when every file is empty).

path.description: Path inside the deliverable version (index.html, assets/logo.svg …), or the shared-files path for shared_download.

chunks.description: Number of file.download frames (0 when the file is empty; at most 20 for the 20 MB limit).

files.description: Exactly one file; path is its shared-files path (data/sample.csv), same rules as the tools' SharedPath.

ToolResult.title: ToolResult
ToolResult.description: Result of a tool.call; ok=false becomes an MCP isError result.

structured.description: Optional structured result matching the tool result schema; null when the tool only returns text.

anchor.description: Set when the call ended the caller's task (complete_task): the new task anchor, "" to clear the stored one (as session.send anchor).

download.description: read_deliverable: files whose bytes arrived before as file.download frames; the daemon writes them under .agent-deliverables/<deliverable_id>/v<version>/ in the session's working directory.

shared_download.description: read_shared_file: the one file whose bytes arrived before as file.download frames; the daemon writes it as .shared/<path> in the session's working directory (the folder holds its own .gitignore).

Welcome.title: Welcome
Welcome.description: Console reply to hello: negotiated protocol and node settings.

protocol.description: Highest version in both protocols lists.

ack_seq.description: Highest daemon seq the console has durably processed (same epoch; 0 when the epoch changed).

min_daemon.description: Older daemons get node.upgrade or close code 4426.

AskLeadInput.title: AskLeadInput
AskLeadInput.description: Ask the thread lead a question and wait for the answer.

AskUserInput.title: AskUserInput
AskUserInput.description: Ask the user a question (a card on the web page). Either a plain question (question + optional options) or up to 4 structured questions (questions: each with a short header, 2-4 options with a description, one may be recommended, multi_select for several answers; the user can always type their own answer instead). Members block until the user answers and get the answer back; the coordinator and leads get the question id at once and receive "[Answer to q5] ..." as a later message. Give question or questions.

question.description: A plain question (use questions for choices with descriptions).

options.description: Suggested answers shown as buttons (with question).

questions.description: Structured questions shown as one card, like Claude Code's AskUserQuestion.

via.description: Set by the platform when Claude's built-in AskUserQuestion is routed here (the call then blocks for every tier). Do not set it yourself.

AssignSubtaskInput.title: AssignSubtaskInput
AssignSubtaskInput.description: Create a subtask of your current task for a teammate (instance or role name); returns the task id at once. Only for roles with can_delegate.

pooled.description: true when assigned to a role (task pool).

AssignTaskInput.title: AssignTaskInput
AssignTaskInput.description: Create a task under a main task. assignee is a role name (dev) to put it in the project's task queue, where an idle member of that role claims it (members are shared by every thread of the project and may be busy in another one), or an instance name (dev-2) to assign it directly (it waits while that member is busy).

main.description: Title of the main task (plan step) this belongs to.

repo.description: Repository the task is about (owner/name); named in the task text. With base, records the thread's base branch in it.

base.description: Base branch the thread uses in repo (only before the thread branch exists there; read the project context for stated bases).

BroadcastInput.title: BroadcastInput
BroadcastInput.description: Send a message to every member of the thread.

CancelTaskInput.title: CancelTaskInput
CancelTaskInput.description: Cancel a task that has not finished.

TaskOutcome.title: TaskOutcome
TaskOutcome.description: Final state of a task that was waited on.

answer.description: Present when the call blocked until answered.

answers.description: Structured questions: the user's choice per question, in order (present when the call blocked until answered).

question.description: The complete question, ending with a question mark.

header.description: Very short label shown as a chip (max 12 characters).

options.description: 2-4 distinct choices; an "other" free-text answer is always offered, do not add one.

multi_select.description: Let the user pick several options.

recommended.description: Mark the option you recommend (at most one per question).

other.description: The user's own answer typed into 其他.

SharedPath.title: SharedPath
SharedPath.description: Path of a file in the project's shared files: relative, '/'-separated, 1 to 8 segments, at most 255 bytes in UTF-8 (the schema can only check 255 characters; the server's byte check is authoritative). No segment may be empty, '.', '..', start with '.' (so no hidden files and nothing under .shared or .agent-*) or start or end with a space; no backslash, control characters (C0, DEL, C1), U+2028/U+2029 or leading '/'.

CompleteTaskInput.title: CompleteTaskInput
CompleteTaskInput.description: Finish your current task explicitly; the platform pushes your branch first. Use status failed when you cannot finish it.

status.description: platform_error: review/decision tasks only, when the platform did not prepare what you were asked to check (for example the worktree HEAD is not the commit under review). It is not a verdict: the platform prepares the review again.

artifacts.description: Paths, commit SHAs or URLs produced by the task.

handoff.description: Note for whoever builds on this task: what is left, pitfalls, interfaces agreed on. Asked for when other tasks depend on this one.

deleted.description: False when no file had this path.

DeleteSharedFileInput.title: DeleteSharedFileInput
DeleteSharedFileInput.description: Delete one of the project's shared files for everyone (copies already fetched into working directories stay). Shared files belong to the project: every session (coordinator, leads, members of all threads) and every user of the project can see, overwrite and delete them; they are stored by the platform, never in git. Do not put secrets (keys, passwords, tokens, credentials) in shared files. A file with the same path is overwritten. Limits: 20 MB per file, 500 MB per project.

EnqueueMergeInput.title: EnqueueMergeInput
EnqueueMergeInput.description: Put a member branch into the merge queue, one entry per repository the task pushed (merged into the thread branch on GitHub, then CI). Give either member or task_id.

repo.description: Merge only this repository of the task (default: every repository the task pushed).

base.description: Base branch the thread uses in repo (only before the thread branch exists there; read the project context for stated bases).

FinishInput.title: FinishInput
FinishInput.description: Write the thread summary; it is also added to the project memory. With code changes, call it after open_pr: the thread ends when the PR merges. A thread that changed no repository (research, review, Q&A) needs no PR: finish ends it right away (done).

ForwardToThreadInput.title: ForwardToThreadInput
ForwardToThreadInput.description: Forward the user's own project-chat messages, word for word with their images, files and @ references, to a thread's lead (thread_no; a finished thread is reopened, an archived one refuses) or into a new thread (new_thread, the messages become its brief). The lead receives them as the user's words; use this instead of paraphrasing when the request belongs to a thread. Each user message ends with [message_id: N]; without message_ids the user's latest messages are forwarded.

new_thread.description: Open a new thread for the messages instead of thread_no.

message_ids.description: The user's messages to forward ([message_id: N] at the end of each), any order.

latest.description: Without message_ids: forward the user's latest N messages (default 1).

note.description: Optional short note of yours sent along (context the lead needs; never a rewrite of the user's words).

GetTaskInput.title: GetTaskInput
GetTaskInput.description: Show a task: instruction, status, dependencies and result.

hosted.description: Files published with publish_file (read_deliverable can fetch them).

thread.description: Thread number; absent for project-level deliverables.

url.description: External link of a deliverable that is not hosted (PR, document elsewhere).

ListDeliverablesInput.title: ListDeliverablesInput
ListDeliverablesInput.description: List this project's deliverables (designs, documents… from every thread), newest first: id, title, kind, versions, who published the latest version, thread and when it changed. Use read_deliverable to fetch one's files.

thread.description: Only deliverables of this thread number.

kind.description: Only this kind (design, doc, slides, dashboard, board, data).

total_bytes.description: Size of all shared files of the project (not only the listed ones).

uploaded_by.description: Employee name, or the user's display name for a web upload; the last writer.

uploaded_by_thread_no.description: Thread number of the employee who wrote it last; absent for users and the coordinator.

ListSharedFilesInput.title: ListSharedFilesInput
ListSharedFilesInput.description: List the project's shared files (path, size, type, checksum, who uploaded it and when), sorted by path, with the project's total size and limit. Shared files belong to the project: every session (coordinator, leads, members of all threads) and every user of the project can see, overwrite and delete them; they are stored by the platform, never in git. Do not put secrets (keys, passwords, tokens, credentials) in shared files. A file with the same path is overwritten. Limits: 20 MB per file, 500 MB per project. Fetch one with read_shared_file, add or replace one with write_shared_file.

prefix.description: Only paths starting with this text (for example data/ or data/2026-).

ListTasksInput.title: ListTasksInput
ListTasksInput.description: List the thread's tasks with assignee, main task, kind and status.

ListTeamInput.title: ListTeamInput
ListTeamInput.description: List the thread team: name, role, type, node and current task of each member.

ListThreadsInput.title: ListThreadsInput
ListThreadsInput.description: List threads, one line each: number, title, status, main-task progress and how many items wait for the user.

MemoryDeleteInput.title: MemoryDeleteInput
MemoryDeleteInput.description: Delete a project memory topic file and its line in MEMORY.md (MEMORY.md itself cannot be deleted).

MemoryListInput.title: MemoryListInput
MemoryListInput.description: List the project's memory files (MEMORY.md and topic files) with their descriptions.

MemoryReadInput.title: MemoryReadInput
MemoryReadInput.description: Read one project memory file in full (MEMORY.md or a topic file listed in it).

MemoryWriteInput.title: MemoryWriteInput
MemoryWriteInput.description: Create or replace a project memory file. A topic file (e.g. testing.md) needs a one-line description; the platform keeps its line in MEMORY.md. name MEMORY.md rewrites the index itself.

MessageThreadInput.title: MessageThreadInput
MessageThreadInput.description: Send a message to a thread's lead as the project coordinator.

pr_number.description: First pull request of the thread.

prs.description: Every pull request of the thread, one per repository.

OpenPrInput.title: OpenPrInput
OpenPrInput.description: Open one pull request per repository the thread changed (thread branch to that repository's base branch); the thread moves to review. Only for code changes: a thread that changed nothing ends with finish alone.

repo.description: Open only this repository's pull request (default: every changed repository without one).

base.description: PR base branch for repo (or for the only repository to open); default the thread's base there.
Base branch for this repository; default its default branch.

OpenThreadInput.title: OpenThreadInput
OpenThreadInput.description: Open a new thread (number, branch, member instances) for a piece of work; the brief becomes the lead's first message. Returns #no immediately.

roles.description: Role names to staff the thread with; default = all member roles of the team.

repos.description: Repositories of the project the thread should work in, with an optional explicit base branch each (when the project context states one).

message_id.description: The user's own message (its [message_id: N]) this thread is opened for; it is shown with the brief and its images and files go to the lead. Default: the user's newest message delivered after your previous reply (none: no message is linked).

PublishDeliverableInput.title: PublishDeliverableInput
PublishDeliverableInput.description: Register a deliverable link for the project (doc, design, slides, dashboard, board, data...). Pull requests are not deliverables (the platform tracks them on the thread).

kind.description: Known: doc, design, slides, dashboard, board, data; anything else is shown as a link. Not pr: pull requests are tracked by the platform on the thread and are not deliverables.

PublishFileInput.title: PublishFileInput
PublishFileInput.description: Publish a file you made (HTML prototype, Markdown doc, PDF, text, JSON, CSV) as a project deliverable. The platform uploads it from your working directory and hosts it; people view it on the Deliverables page and their comments come back to you as messages. A directory with index.html is published as a small site (it may contain images and other assets). Pass deliverable_id to publish a new version of an earlier deliverable. Screenshots and images are not deliverables: a lone PNG/JPG/GIF/WebP is saved as an attachment in your thread's messages instead (no deliverable, cannot be a new version), and a lone SVG is refused. To put an image in a report, publish it in one directory with the report's index.html, or inline it in the HTML (an SVG can be written straight into the HTML); Markdown cannot show images. Cite an attachment (its id or URL) only in your written report.

path.description: File (or directory with index.html) inside your working directory, relative to it.

kind.description: design for prototypes and visual designs, doc for documents and specs; also slides, dashboard, board, data.

deliverable_id.description: An earlier deliverable of this project published with publish_file; the file becomes its next version.

head_sha.description: Head of the first pushed repository ("" when nothing was pushed).

PushBranchInput.title: PushBranchInput
PushBranchInput.description: Push the HEAD of each of your repository checkouts that has new commits to your member branch (thread/<no>/<name>). You have no write token yourself; commit first, then call this.

dir.description: Folder relative to your working directory (the daemon adds the absolute path).

entry.description: The file a viewer opens (index.html of a site, or the only file).

thread.description: Thread number of the employee who published it.

ReadDeliverableInput.title: ReadDeliverableInput
ReadDeliverableInput.description: Fetch the files of a deliverable published with publish_file (any thread of this project) into your working directory under .agent-deliverables/<id>/v<version>/ (git-ignored; a multi-file site keeps its folders). Returns the local folder, the file list, the version history and the user's comments. To revise it: edit the files there, then publish_file(path=<that folder or file>, deliverable_id=<id>) to publish the next version.

version.description: Version to fetch; the latest when omitted.

ReadMessagesInput.title: ReadMessagesInput
ReadMessagesInput.description: Return your unread messages (including broadcasts) and mark them read.

local_path.description: Where the file was written, relative to your working directory: .shared/<path> (the daemon adds the absolute path). Read the file there with your file tools.

ReadSharedFileInput.title: ReadSharedFileInput
ReadSharedFileInput.description: Download one of the project's shared files to .shared/<path> in your working directory (the folder is git-ignored) and return that local path; the result never contains the file's content, so read it with your file tools. Shared files belong to the project: every session (coordinator, leads, members of all threads) and every user of the project can see, overwrite and delete them; they are stored by the platform, never in git. Do not put secrets (keys, passwords, tokens, credentials) in shared files. An existing local copy at the same path is overwritten. Limits: 20 MB per file, 500 MB per project. To change the shared file, edit the local copy and call write_shared_file(file=.shared/<path>).

path.description: Path in the shared files, for example data/sample.csv (see list_shared_files).

RememberInput.title: RememberInput
RememberInput.description: Append a one-line note to the project memory index MEMORY.md (shortcut for small facts).

ReplyToInput.title: ReplyToInput
ReplyToInput.description: Answer a member's question ("[Question q3 from dev-1 ...]"). Answer quickly: the member is blocked until you do.

ReportProgressInput.title: ReportProgressInput
ReportProgressInput.description: Report progress on your task (shown in the thread activity).

RequestReviewInput.title: RequestReviewInput
RequestReviewInput.description: Ask a teammate to review your work (creates a review task under your current task) and wait for the result. You cannot ask yourself.

ReviewPermissionInput.title: ReviewPermissionInput
ReviewPermissionInput.description: Decide a member's permission request ("[Permission request q5 from dev-1 ...]"). allow lets the member run it once, deny refuses it (the reason goes to the member), ask_user hands it to the user. Choose ask_user when unsure, or when it touches secrets, production, money, other people or anything irreversible. Decide quickly: the member waits.

reason.description: One sentence; shown to the user in the thread's activity and on the card.

SendMessageInput.title: SendMessageInput
SendMessageInput.description: Leave a message for a teammate (instance name) or for the lead ("lead"). Busy recipients get it after their current turn.

SetStatusInput.title: SetStatusInput
SetStatusInput.description: Set your speech-bubble text in the office (one short sentence on what you are doing). Call it when you switch work; it does not change your state or position and expires after 10 minutes.

TellUserInput.title: TellUserInput
TellUserInput.description: Post a short message to the user in the thread conversation right away (shown as the lead's own message), without ending the turn. Use it for the receipt after the brief and for updates the user should see; it is not a question (use ask_user to ask).

ThreadStatusInput.title: ThreadStatusInput
ThreadStatusInput.description: Show one thread: plan, recent activity, the lead's latest reply and the PR.

UpdatePlanInput.title: UpdatePlanInput
UpdatePlanInput.description: Replace the thread plan (main tasks). Steps are matched by title so existing main tasks keep their ids.

WaitTaskInput.title: WaitTaskInput
WaitTaskInput.description: Wait until one of your subtasks finishes and return its result. Only for roles with can_delegate.

overwritten.description: True when a file with this path existed and was replaced.

WriteSharedFileInput.title: WriteSharedFileInput
WriteSharedFileInput.description: Upload one file from your working directory to the project's shared files (store data, samples, exports other sessions or users need; not deliverables, use publish_file for those). Shared files belong to the project: every session (coordinator, leads, members of all threads) and every user of the project can see, overwrite and delete them; they are stored by the platform, never in git. Do not put secrets (keys, passwords, tokens, credentials) in shared files. A file with the same path is overwritten. Limits: 20 MB per file, 500 MB per project.

file.description: A single file inside your working directory, relative to it (directories are refused).

path.description: Target path in the shared files. Default: file normalised to a relative path, with a leading .shared/ removed (so a file fetched with read_shared_file goes back to the same path).
